narrative.overview:
**Creative North Star: "Warm Logic"**

Technical sharpness with warmth: the site must feel capable and approachable at the same time. The logic is in the structure. A strict type scale, one content column, flat fields of colour that turn the page into chapters, and the product drawn as exact UI, not as a mood picture. The warmth is in the materials. Each neutral is tinted with the hue of its theme (never grey). The accents are soft and slightly dusty, not neon. The headlines speak in two tones, as a person who says the claim and then adds the honest aside. Small text faces (`[••]`, `[•ᴥ•]`, `[•*•]`) wink at the end of a line.

Density is generous on marketing surfaces: big type, much air, one idea for each field of colour. The page is a vertical flow of full-bleed bands. Each band commits to one surface (the pale page, the bright accent or the deep inverse). Splits of two halves (accent | inverse) carry a claim on one side and its proof on the other. Depth does not exist: the change from one surface to the next is the only layering.

This system came from overnice's work ("Warm Logic" is their name for the route), merged with the needs of the old site. It is still in progress. The reference pages above are the evidence. The other pages are not.
keyCharacteristics: Six themes (default, orange, green, purple, blue, pink). Each is a set of three surfaces: a near-white paper, a bright accent and a deep inverse, in the hue of the accent (the deep of the default, green and purple themes is a neighbouring hue: see Colors). The docs have a seventh theme of their own (see "The docs theme").
Full-bleed bands of flat colour; a theme changes from section to section, never inside a component.
Two-tone headlines: the claim in the text colour, then the aside in a muted tone of the same hue.
One sans (ABC Oracle) at two weights, tight negative tracking; Geist Mono for code and product chrome: 500 in code blocks, and on the page 400 on light grounds and 500 on dark grounds.
Pill buttons with an arrow; instant hover that swaps the two colours.
The product as code-rendered scenes, cut off by the edge of the band, with a top-left corner radius only.
Pixel art as the playful signature: pixel videos of hands and people in the page closer, a pixel hover on photos.
Diagrams with one grammar (pill, track, pulse, ring) for what the product does when it is not a screen.

rules.name: The One Hue Rule
rules.body: A section uses the three tones of one family. Two accents of different themes never touch inside a section; they meet only at the edge between two bands.

rules.name: The Role Not Colour Rule
rules.body: Components use only semantic tokens (`--surface-*`, `--text-*`, `--border-*`), named for their role. A hex in a component is a bug.

rules.name: The Dark Text On Accent Rule
rules.body: All six accents are light. Text on a bright accent is the deep tone. In the dark scheme the accent band is deep, and its text is light; a small bright accent shape keeps the deep tone.

rules.name: The Two-Tone Rule
rules.body: A headline says the claim in the text colour, then continues in the quiet run: `--text-headline-muted`, the headline-muted role of the ground (the muted text on the page, a lighter step on the accent and the inverse, at 3:1 or more because the headline is large text). "Modular how you like it. _And steady how you need it._" The muted half never gets its own size or weight. This is the main voice of the site.

rules.name: The Two Weights Rule
rules.body: ABC Oracle at 400 and 500 only. `strong` is 500. No bold, no italic as decoration, no uppercase tracking except the mono caps role. The product scenes kit renders at the weight 340 of the cms, inside the pictures only.

rules.name: The Text Face Rule
rules.body: A hero headline can end with a text face (`[••]`, `[•ᴥ•]`, `[•*•]`), joined to the last word so that it never wraps alone. The typewriter can type it and make it wink. One face for each headline, at most. The face is our voice, and it follows an aside: the headline is a full sentence (it ends with `.`, `?` or `!`), and the muted run adds to it ("Got issues? We're here to help! [••]"). A title in two tones ("Projects from Our / Partners") has no face. The copy names the face (`face` in `src/data`). The hero adds no face by default. Text from the CMS (a plugin, a starter, a partner), a title alone and a legal page have no face. Each page closer with a call to action ends its headline with a face: the page selects it (`<PageCloser face="…">`, a name from `src/lib/motion/faces.ts`) to fit its subject, and the face plays when it comes into view. The closer face is not the face of the hero of the same page. Each face plays its animation, always: in a typewriter script (`faceStep`), or with the `Face` component (`<Face name="…">`), which plays it when it comes into view, on load, or each time a form error shows. A hero without the typewriter, a section headline, a form message: all use `Face`. No component writes the glyphs of a face, and no copy has them. The library has more than 30 faces, thus the faces do not repeat: each face is on 2 heroes or closers at most, on different pages, and each one fits its copy (its `description` in `faces.ts` tells where). The pages of one template (the `/cms` pages) count as one. The 404 has `confused`. `/dev/face-gallery` shows them all.

rules.name: The Hero Length Rule
rules.body: The h1 of a hero (the headline, the muted run and the face) has 120 characters at most: 3 lines on a desktop, 6 on a phone. A longer description goes in the `intro`, as body text below the h1, not in the muted run. `src/lib/hero.test.ts` checks the copy of `src/data` and the Hero calls of `src/pages` (the length, the face after a sentence, each face on 2 places at most, no face glyphs outside `faces.ts`, the glyphs read only by the components that play them, the typewriter on the marketing pages only); the dev server warns when text from the CMS goes over.

rules.name: The Same Hue At Both Ends Rule
rules.body: The header, the hero, the page closer and the footer have the theme of the page. Two inverse surfaces of different hues never touch.

rules.name: The Full Bleed Rule
rules.body: A coloured surface reaches the edges of the viewport. A coloured box that floats in the column with page margins around it is not part of this system.

rules.name: The Flat, No Exceptions Rule
rules.body: No `box-shadow` with blur, no `drop-shadow`, no glow, in the site and in the docs. There are no shadow tokens. A photo in a diagram has no shadow and no ring.

dos: **Do** give each section one theme and one surface, full bleed, and change the theme only between bands.
**Do** give each page the theme of its area (a reference page) or of its first chapter (a marketing page), and let the header, the hero, the closer and the footer take it.
**Do** write headlines in two tones: the claim, then the muted aside.
**Do** use the split (accent half | inverse half) to put a claim next to its proof.
**Do** show the product as a code-rendered scene, cut by the edge of the band, with only its top-left corner rounded.
**Do** use only the semantic tokens and the `--space-*` and `--type-*` scales, and check every change in both schemes.
**Do** give the element that paints a band its ground class (`surfaceAccent`, `surfaceInverse`, `surfacePage`), and set `color` to a role of that ground in the same rule as the background.
**Do** keep motion short and in view only: 150 to 400ms, ease-out or cubic-bezier(0.3, 0, 0, 1), and the final state without JS. Diagrams use their own two curves and step one thing at a time.
**Do** draw a new diagram with the shared grammar (`src/scenes/diagram/`): pill, track, pulse, panel, ring, one accent.
**Do** put a pixel video only in the page closer, with a palette from `src/lib/pixel-video/styles.ts`.
donts: **Don't** use a shadow of any kind, also on popovers and product windows.
**Don't** use grey. Every neutral is the deep of the theme at an alpha.
**Don't** dim text with `opacity` or `color-mix()`. The quiet text is `--text-muted`; the quiet run of a headline is `--text-headline-muted`.
**Don't** round a band, a cell or a half, or float a coloured box with margins inside the column.
**Don't** put light text on a bright accent: all six accents take the deep text. (In the dark scheme the accent band is deep and its text is light: `surfaceAccent` does it.)
**Don't** add a third font weight, a bold, a tracked uppercase text outside the mono caps role or a second typeface for display.
**Don't** use screenshots, stock photos or AI imagery where a scene, pixel art or a real customer photo can go.
**Don't** mix two accents of different themes inside one section.
**Don't** give the header, the closer or the footer a theme that is not the theme of the page, and don't put a hero on the inverse.
**Don't** use arrows, dashed lines, red or a second accent in a diagram.
**Don't** give a pixel video colours of its own, a blur or a tone curve: a new look is a new palette.
**Don't** take a pattern from a page that is not in the reference list (see the comment at the top) without asking.
